pr_body:
Adds a lock around the logger backend for adsp and changes the buffer size to 80 to avoid 1 character a time writes to the trace buffer

fixes #44145
pr_comments: Even with CONFIG_LOG_PRINTK=y there's garbled output in the provided sample prior to this fix. Maybe not the  best way to fix this and I'm open to suggestions, but the fix does in fact solve a problem
Then maybe there's missing synchronization in the logging subsystem?

Possibly, the lock around winstream is fine (in trace_out.c) but it effectively is locking character at a time given the way printk works and the log output is setup (1 character size). Which means its very possible for two messages to get mixed up.

But beyond that there also seems to be perhaps a race in how the log backend is used itself. It doesn't seem like there's any serialization on the backend, e.g. process may be called from two contexts and corrupt the output. Something to do with log_core's panic mode flag perhaps? Since in panic mode all log calls are then processed in the context of the log call. In a SMP system this won't prevent the background log thread from continuing to happily pump out log data perhaps from the currently in process message.

I don't disagree this isn't a pretty fix, marking DNM for now, but at least something of a solution (and perhaps a cause) is known now. Will sit on it and sort out a better answer perhaps.

I believe I fully grok the issue(s) now and the commit message reflects all the races I found and how to avoid them, along with a lock around process() in particular avoiding the race and buffer trampling.

The output looks good.
There's potentially an alternative fix by putting a lock around the body of z_impl_log_process though I'm not sure of all the implications.

> This seems to address the problem indeed! I did note following weird output when I had also #44529 included. It's still readable, but ordering is unexpected.

> @nordic-krch had good comments, but other than that, looks good to me.

I believe this is because printk is used to print the backtrace, which can lead to other issues. CONFIG_LOG_PRINTK=y should solve this. There's no shared lock between the two to prevent a message from printk and log becoming entwined, the preferred solution as @andyross mentions above is to let the logger process printk to avoid that. I've done some additions in this PR to partially address the issue and at least make it readable by having the logger output larger contiguous messages (up to 80 bytes) rather than the character at a time it was doing before.

And right: per the discussion above, if there's desire to use printk() in application code alongside the logging macros, we almost certainly want to set CONFIG_LOG_PRINTK=y so that printk() is implemented in terms of logging.  Having both trace subsystems active at once is allowed, but really only useful for special purposes (e.g. you might be debugging one by using the other), and we don't want them interacting more than is absolutely required.  I think interleaving between the two seems acceptable to me given the obvious workaround.

> And right: per the discussion above, if there's desire to use printk() in application code alongside the logging macros, we

I can confirm this to be the case. With CONFIG_LOG_PRINTK (and this PR), the OS panic is clean including the backtrace. Submitted https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/44684 to enable this for SOF builds.

review_comments: have you considered to put this lock in `char_out` around `intel_adsp_trace_out`. Here it will lock for significant amount of time in the lower priority thread (in case of deferred mode). Putting it in `char_out` may lead to some interleaving of data within the log message so there is a trade off.

There's already a lock in intel_adsp_trace_out

That was one of the problems being solved here, on the intel_adsp with a fatal exception ISR being run on one cpu, the lower priority logger thread continues to run on another and tramples the data.

I was debating if a lock should be placed around the body of z_impl_log_process in log_core.c instead as it seems there's a race when panic mode and the log thread collide on SMP systems.

What I wasn't sure of is if that's the right place or not, that's I think something you could help sort out @nordic-krch
